title: Etale algebra maps lift across an arbitrary locally nilpotent ideal
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring with identity, and let $C,T$ be commutative unital $A$-algebras, allowing zero rings. Suppose that $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale [def-weil-affine-spectrum], [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Let $J\subseteq T$ be an ideal every element of which is nilpotent, meaning that for each $t\in J$ there exists an integer $n\geq1$ with $t^n=0$. For every unital $A$-algebra homomorphism $g:C\to T/J$, there exists a unital $A$-algebra homomorphism $h:C\to T$ such that $q\circ h=g$, where $q:T\to T/J$ is the quotient map. No uniform exponent annihilating $J$ and no Noetherian assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tag 07K4, label lemma-smooth-strong-lift, specialized to etale (hence smooth) ring maps; the affine translation is lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine], the given affine etale morphism implies that $C$ is finitely presented over $A$, $H_1(L_{C/A})=0$, and $\Omega_{C/A}=0$. Thus $\Omega_{C/A}$ is projective: the zero module is a direct summand of the free module of rank zero. Using the explicit meaning of finite presentation in [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], fix an $A$-algebra presentation $C=A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$ with $n,m\geq0$. These are exactly the cotangent hypotheses needed for square-zero lifting below.

source.place: Tags 00U1 and 00T2 (definition-smooth), as used to specialize Tag 07K4 to etale maps

proof.text: For each $i$ choose $t_i\in T$ lifting $g(\overline{x_i})$. Evaluate polynomials over $A$ at the $t_i$ using the fixed structure map $A\to T$. Put $e_j=f_j(t_1,\ldots,t_n)$. Reduction modulo $J$ gives $g(f_j(\overline{x}))=0$, so $e_j\in J$. Set $K=(e_1,\ldots,e_m)\subseteq J$. Evaluation modulo $K$ kills every relation and hence their generated ideal; it therefore induces a unital $A$-algebra map $g_1:C\to T/K$. Its composite with $T/K\to T/J$ agrees with $g$ on the generators and on $A$, hence on every polynomial class.

source.place: Tag 07K4 (lemma-smooth-strong-lift); agent finite-relations reduction in place of Noetherian descent

proof.text: Choose integers $d_j\geq1$ with $e_j^{d_j}=0$, using $e_j\in J$. Set $M=1+\sum_{j=1}^m(d_j-1)$. Each element of $K^M$ is a finite sum of multiples of monomials $e_1^{a_1}\cdots e_m^{a_m}$ with $\sum a_j=M$; some $a_j\geq d_j$ by the displayed formula for $M$, so every monomial is zero. Thus $K^M=0$. If $m=0$, then $K=0$ and $M=1$, and the same conclusion holds. Only the finitely many $e_j$ require exponents; no exponent for $J$ has been chosen.

source.place: Tag 07K4; elementary finite-relations replacement of the source reduction to a nilpotent ideal

proof.text: Inductively construct unital $A$-algebra maps $g_r:C\to T/K^r$ for $1\leq r\leq M$, whose reductions to $T/K$ are $g_1$, starting with the map in step 2. For $r<M$, let $D=T/K^{r+1}$ and let $N$ be the image of $K^r$ in $D$. Products from $N$ vanish because $K^{2r}\subseteq K^{r+1}$ for $r\geq1$. The map $D\to T/K^r$, $t\bmod K^{r+1}\mapsto t\bmod K^r$, is surjective with kernel $N$; it gives an $A$-algebra isomorphism $D/N\cong T/K^r$, since equality of classes on either side means difference in $K^r$. Regard $g_r$ as a map into $D/N$ through this isomorphism. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-square-zero-lifting] with $B=C$ and the cotangent hypotheses of step 1. It yields $g_{r+1}:C\to D$ whose reduction to $T/K^r$ is $g_r$. Its reduction to $T/K$ is consequently $g_1$, completing the induction.

source.place: Tag 07K4, final successive-lifting paragraph; Tag 031J (proposition-characterize-formally-smooth), (6) implies (1), and Tag 00TI

proof.text: Since $K^M=0$, sending $t\bmod K^M$ to $t$ is a unital $A$-algebra isomorphism $T/K^M\cong T$. Compose $g_M$ with it to obtain $h:C\to T$. The reduction of $g_M$ to $T/K$ is $g_1$ by the induction, and $g_1$ reduces to $g$ modulo $J$ by step 2. Hence $q\circ h=g$. If $M=1$, the induction has no successor step and this same calculation applies directly to $g_1$.

source.place: Tag 07K4, last sentence; quotient-map compatibility written explicitly
